item.description:
### Added
- lika has its own app icon, shown in Finder and Launchpad. - A phone with Phone Link can choose which Stems a Recording holds, as the Recording page does, and sees the choice change wherever it's made. - A phone can rename a Recording on the Mac, and its Cancel after stopping a Recording moves that Recording to the Trash, where you can put it back. A phone can't remove any other Recording.

### Added
- Drag the Overlay by the pill between its circles to anywhere along any edge of the screen, or of another display, such as the top right corner: while you drag, an outline shows where it will land, turning between a row and a column, and on release it snaps to the edge it is nearest, centring itself when you let go near the middle. On the left or right edge the Overlay is a column, with its Quick Controls and Overlay Messages opening beside it. The General page's position picker has all four edges too, and centres the Overlay on the one you pick. - Remote control, a new page in the Settings Window, pairs phones with the lika app by QR code and lists them with Disconnect and Remove. Each new phone asks "Allow this phone?" beside the Overlay, and the Overlay shows a phone icon while Phone Link is on, lit with the number of phones connected. - While Room Tune measures, the Overlay Message says "Room measurement in progress", whether the measurement started on the Mac or on a phone, and it goes away when the measurement ends. - With Phone Link on, a phone on the same network can change the sound live, read the meters and spectrum, start and stop a Recording, apply its own Presets or save them to Preset 1, 2 or 3, and download your Recordings, Stems included, resuming after a dropped connection. Downloads pause while the Mac records. Phone Link is off until you switch it on, and with it off lika opens no network port. - A phone with Phone Link can measure Room Tune, cancel the measurement or delete its cuts, and follows every measurement as it runs, wherever it started. A measurement carries on if the phone that started it disconnects.
### Changed
- The Quick Controls are one set for every Mic Channel, as the Effects page already was: a slider or switch changes every Mic Channel, whichever Mic Badge you opened them from, and a phone shows and sets the same values. Channel Bypass, gain and Channel Mute stay each Mic Channel's own. A Preset saved with different effect settings per Mic Channel loads with Mic Channel 1's on every one.
### Fixed
- Measuring Room Tune ends at once when a device disconnects, saying so, or when the devices change, such as a new buffer size, and the cuts you had are kept. It used to carry on and fail later as if nothing had howled, or start over by itself.

### Added
- A Noise Gate, which silences a Mic Channel below a cutoff and fades the voice back in over a smoothness you set, with a live picture of where your voice sits on it. Its mix sets how far it lowers the voice. - A Chorus, which adds one to four voices of your own across the stereo Output, with their delay, modulation, width and mix. Its mix is also a slider in the Quick Controls. - A Saturator, which adds tube or tape warmth in three bands with their own intensity, split at crossovers you drag on its picture over the live mic spectrum. Its amount is also a slider in the Quick Controls. - Recordings: press the record button in the Overlay, or ⌃⌥R from any app, to record, and again to stop. The Overlay shows the time recorded, and a saved Recording's Overlay Message shows it in Finder. - On the new Recording page, choose the Stems a Recording holds, in any combination: the Output mix, each Mic Channel wet (with its effects and its own reverb), each Mic Channel dry, and the Backing Track at its own level while it passes through lika. The Output mix alone is one .m4a file. Anything more is a folder holding `Mix.m4a` and a WAV file for every other Stem, all starting on the same sample. - Recordings are saved in `~/Music/lika`, named by the date and time they started. A full disk, a device change or quitting lika stops the Recording and saves it.
### Changed
- The Effects page edits one Vocal Chain for every Mic Channel, numbered in the order your voice meets it: Noise Gate, compressor, EQ, Chorus, de-esser, Saturator. Each effect's on/off button there is also a knob for its Quick Controls slider: click it to switch the effect, scroll over it to turn the slider. The Reverb Bus has one for the reverb mix. Each effect folds down to its name, that button and Reset when you click its header. Each Mic Channel's Quick Controls are still its own, and Copy to all Mic Channels is gone. - The compressor now comes before the EQ, so it no longer reacts to what the EQ boosts; a Preset with both on may sound slightly different. - The Quick Controls sliders follow the Vocal Chain's order, Comp before EQ. - The Example Track plays through the first Mic Channel, with each effect on or off as you set it rather than switching the EQ, compressor, de-esser and reverb on. - The Feedback Suppressor now predicts howls: one still building up steadily, too quiet to hear yet, is cut before it gets loud. Howls that start suddenly are caught as before. - The Feedback Suppressor catches a howl that comes back as its cut lifts, or soon after, much faster, and a cut already at its deepest widens to reach a howl just beside it. - The Settings Window opens at General, and its sidebar now reads General, Devices, Recording, then Effects, Master, Presets, then System. Master output is now Master, and Updates is now System. - The Overlay sits centred at the top or bottom of the screen instead of in a corner. If you had it in a corner, it stays on that side of the screen. - The Overlay shows small until the mouse comes close, then grows to full size, and shrinks again when the mouse leaves. - Quick Controls open centred on the Overlay and as wide as it, rather than beside their Mic Badge.
### Fixed
- The Feedback Suppressor no longer misses a howl when another peak sits just beside it. - The Feedback Suppressor no longer lets a howl grow loud when the room rings at whole multiples of its frequency, or while several howls build at once. In a real room, howls are now cut long before they can be heard. - The Feedback Suppressor now also stops a howl set off by a knock or a shout when the gain is already past where the room howls, and a cut goes in at full depth within 50 ms.

### Added
- The Backing Track can pass through lika. Turn it on and choose the Backing Track Source on the Devices page, from the apps open with a Dock icon. Its music is then mixed into the Output beside the Mic Channels, with no effects or Feedback Suppressor on it and untouched by Bypass, while Mute and the master level apply to it. Turning it on or off never interrupts the microphones or adds to their Round-Trip Latency. lika remembers the app and captures it again whenever it reopens. It needs macOS 14.2 and asks once for permission to capture app audio. - The Backing Track Badge in the Overlay shows the music's level and sets it with a scroll or a drag; a click mutes the music alone. Presets keep the Backing Track's level. - The Devices page shows the latency passing the Backing Track through lika adds to the music.

The first Release of lika: live effects for up to two karaoke microphones on an Apple Silicon Mac, sitting above whatever you sing along to and adding under 0.1 ms of Processing Latency.
### Added
#### Microphones and sound
- Up to two Mic Channels, each mapped onto an Input Channel of your Input Device, with its own gain, EQ, compressor and de-esser and a send to the shared Reverb Bus. Every effect works sample by sample, with no look-ahead. - The EQ has a low cut or shelf, three bells and a high shelf or cut. Cuts are 12, 18 or 24 dB/oct, and the EQ amount morphs every band towards flat. - The Reverb Bus is one reverb that every Mic Channel feeds, with its own decay and settings. - The Output ends in a 19 kHz low pass and a limiter that caps it at −1 dBFS, always on and with no look-ahead. - Bypass passes every Mic Channel through with its gain only, and Channel Bypass does that for one Mic Channel. Both fade over 50 ms. - Mute (⌃⌥M, or a hotkey of your choice) silences everything at once, as an emergency stop for a howl. Channel Mute silences one Mic Channel. - lika runs at 96 kHz and a 64-sample buffer by default, the lowest Device Latency that runs clean with every effect on.
#### Feedback protection
- The Feedback Suppressor finds a howl while you sing and cuts just that frequency until the howl has gone, telling it apart from a held sung note. There is one on each Mic Channel and a less sensitive one on the master mix. It catches high howls soonest, cuts up to 30 dB deep and lets go within 5 s of the howl stopping. One sensitivity setting drives them all, and it keeps working in Bypass. - The Mic Badges and the master control glow green, amber or red with how hard the Feedback Suppressor is cutting. - Room Tune, on the Master output page: hold a microphone in front of the speaker, click Tune, and for 15 s from the first howl lika notes where the Feedback Suppressor had to cut. It then cuts the master mix there by up to 12 dB, the worst frequencies the most. It belongs to the room rather than a Preset, is kept until you tune again or delete it, and Bypass skips it. - The Master output page shows what each Feedback Suppressor hears and which frequencies it is cutting, live.
#### The Overlay
- The Overlay stays above fullscreen video in a screen corner of your choice: the preset button, a Mic Badge per Mic Channel, the master output control and the settings icon. - A Mic Badge's ring shows its Mic Channel's level. Scroll or drag it to change the gain, and click it for Channel Mute. - Hovering a Mic Badge opens its Quick Controls: one slider and switch per effect, and Channel Bypass. - The Overlay Message shows what needs your attention, one message at a time. - An optional latency mark in the master control's ring colours with the Round-Trip Latency, green when it is low.
#### The Settings Window
- Devices, Effects, Master output, Presets, General and Updates pages, shaped like macOS System Settings. - Devices: pick the Input Device, map each Mic Channel, pick the Output pair and buffer size, see the latency broken down, measure the Round-Trip Latency and watch the DSP load. - Effects: a tab per Mic Channel and one for the Reverb Bus. The EQ curve's handles drag, scroll and double-click. The compressor and de-esser curves show what they are doing right now, and the EQ and de-esser curves show the signal moving beneath them. - Example Tracks: a raw a cappella vocal per genre (Rock, Pop, Calm) plays through one Mic Channel's effects in place of its microphone, so you can tune them without singing.
#### Presets
- The Session Slot always holds your latest changes, and three Preset Slots each ship with a factory Preset you can overwrite. Everything is kept across relaunches. - Loading a Preset glides to it over a time you set, up to 2 s.
#### Devices
- lika follows your Input Device and Output Device when they change or disappear, and mutes itself when it has to fall back to devices you didn't choose. - At launch lika asks for microphone permission if macOS hasn't asked yet. When it's denied, an Overlay Message says lika can't hear, and its button opens Privacy & Security → Microphone.
#### Updates
- lika checks for a new Release at launch, downloads it in the background and installs it when you quit or restart it, never during a Session. "Check now" on the Updates page only checks: an Update it finds waits for you to click Download, then "Restart and install". - The Updates page shows the version, when lika last checked, the "Check automatically at launch" and "Include betas" switches, and the release notes of every newer Release. - If lika runs from outside Applications, an Overlay Message offers to move it there, so that it can receive Updates.

item.title: 1.0.0-beta.3
item.description:
### Changed
- Nothing you would notice: this beta exists to check that lika installs its own Updates.

item.title: 1.0.0-beta.2
item.description:
### Fixed
- The Overlay and the Settings Window stayed empty when lika ran straight from Downloads or from any folder under `/private`, as macOS does with a freshly downloaded app.

item.title: 1.0.0-beta.1
item.description:
### Added
- The first beta of lika: live processing for up to two microphones on an Apple Silicon Mac, adding 0 ms of Processing Latency. - Each Mic Channel has gain, a Feedback Suppressor, an EQ, a compressor and a de-esser, plus a send to the shared Reverb Bus. An always-on limiter and Mute (⌃⌥M) protect the output. - The Overlay stays above fullscreen video: one row with the preset button, a Mic Badge per Mic Channel, the master output control and the settings icon. Hovering a Mic Badge opens its Quick Controls, and the Overlay Message shows what needs your attention. - The Settings Window has Devices, Effects, Master output, Presets, General and Updates pages. Devices shows the latency breakdown and can measure Round-Trip Latency. - Presets: the Session Slot plus three Preset Slots, kept across relaunches. - lika follows your Input Device and Output Device when they change or disappear, and mutes itself when a pinned device goes missing. - Updates: lika checks for a new version at launch and when you ask, downloads it in the background, and installs it when you quit, or at once from the "lika X is ready" Overlay Message. It never installs while lika runs. - The Updates page in the Settings Window shows the version and build, "Check for updates", when lika last checked, the "Check automatically at launch" and "Include betas" switches, and the release notes of every newer Release. - If lika runs from outside Applications, an Overlay Message offers to move it there, so that it can receive Updates. - At launch lika asks for microphone permission if macOS hasn't asked yet. When it's denied, an error Overlay Message says lika can't hear, and its System Settings button opens Privacy & Security → Microphone.
### Changed
- lika's bundle identifier is now `com.lpi.lika`, so macOS asks once more for microphone permission.
